facts.text: Federated Co-operatives Limited is investing more than $150 million in its 2026 turnaround at the Regina Co-op Refinery Complex, a facility that employs more than 970 people.
Cargill's new canola crush facility in Regina supports approximately 100 full-time jobs and contractors and adds to Western Canada's canola processing capacity.
Regina's labour market remains among the strongest in Canada, with employment growth forecast at 1.7 percent and unemployment falling to 5.3 percent in 2025.
The largest employers in Regina are the provincial government and its Crown corporations, including SaskTel and Saskatchewan Government Insurance.
Major private sector employers in Regina include Evraz Inc., western Canada's largest steel manufacturer, along with Brandt Industries, Viterra and Bayer CropScience.

overview: Regina's population reached 226,404 in the 2021 Census, a 5.3 percent rise from 215,106 in 2016. The median household income of $88,000 in 2020 sits above the national figure, the median age is 37.6, and 92,129 occupied private dwellings are spread across 178.81 square kilometres.

For a local business, that combination means a stable, well-paid customer base anchored by the provincial government, Crown corporations and steady industrial employers such as the Co-op refinery and Evraz. Growth is moderate, so winning customers depends on visibility and trust rather than riding a boom.
